brief: Distinguish an index-tracking strategy from a promise to beat the market.

title.es-MX: Seguir un índice no es prometer
title.pt-BR: Seguir um índice não é prometer

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Index Tracking"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Seguir un índice no es prometer"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Seguir um índice não é prometer"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Distinguish an index-tracking strategy from a promise to beat the market.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A strategy explains what a fund tries to follow; it does not promise to outperform or avoid losses.
instruction.misconception: Index tracking promises to beat the index, avoid losses or match it exactly after costs.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: An index tracks a defined basket. An index fund aims to follow that basket, with fees and tracking differences possible.
Tracking aims to follow, not promise superiority.
Following a falling basket can include losses.
Fees can reduce the fund’s result relative to its index.
The selected index determines the exposure being followed.
Tracking alone cannot support a promise of always outperforming.
The tracked baskets create different underlying exposures.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
